study: Landry et al. 2021, remote eTEEM teacher PD x ePALS (2x2 factorial), Head Start pre-k (ECRQ)
eval_evidence: Remote-delivery replication conducted/authored by the Children's Learning Institute team that developed eTEEM/ePALS (IES R305A140386); developers ran and reported the evaluation.
developer_evidence: eTEEM online courses + remote coaching delivered by project coaches trained by senior research staff over multiple training days (p.697, 728); program built via 'partnership between the researchers' (p.257).
cascade_evidence: Research-team-trained project coaches deliver online coaching directly to teachers remotely; no school lead-teacher train-the-trainer cascade.
counterfactual_evidence: TPD contrast = eTEEM main effect; 'No eTEEM' = control/business as usual (n=33 classrooms) (abstract p.43-45, p.297-298). ePALS is a separate crossed parent factor.
coaching_evidence: eTEEM = 14 online course sessions + up to 14 individualized remote coaching sessions, approximately biweekly Nov-April (~3 hr/month), each cycle co-viewing/reflecting on videotaped classroom activities (p.808-851).
student_dose_evidence: TPD-vs-control contrast = eTEEM main effect (teacher PD) only; ePALS is a separate crossed parent-directed home program, collapsed across in the eTEEM main effect; no direct student tutoring/software dose.
maturity_evidence: Children measured pre-post across one Head Start pre-k year; single-academic-year school-readiness program with no multi-year maturation axis.
